newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Ericsson hits high.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Ericsson hits high.

text.p: Swedish telephone equipment maker Telefon AB L.M. Ericsson hit a 12-month high Thursday to stand out among American Depositary Receipts (ADRs).

Boosted by strong earnings, Ericsson rose 3-1/2 to 45-1/4, above its closing high of 44-12/16. The ADRs had risen as high as 46-5/8 before easing and Ericsson was among the most-active issues on the Nasdaq exchange.
Fellow Nordic telecommunications equipment maker Nokia Group also was up, rising 3-3/8 to 81-7/8.
"Everything was just going on all cylinders at Ericsson and that just spilled over into Nokia," said Val Kosmider, head of international equity trading at Schroder Wertheim.
Ericsson reported a surprising 44 percent rise in pre-tax earnings Thursday. BellSouth Corp also announced it
had awarded a $200 million contract to Ericsson.

Dutch software company Baan Co fell five to 70-3/4 in trade that by late morning was three times normal daily levels. The drop came after the company reported second-quarter earnings per share of $0.17 against $0.07 for the same year before.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and Smith Barney reduced their ratings for Baan in the earnings' aftermath.
Fellow Dutch company Philips Electronics NV rose 4-4/16 to 82-15/16, a 12-month high, after the company reported better-than-expected second-quarter results.
Among Latin American ADRs, Telefonos de Mexico rose 5/8 to 51-3/8. It was among the most-active issues on the New York Stock Exchange.
ADRs allow U.S. trade of foreign shares.
